summary: Seed adopter required-checks from a template, not from the hub instance

delivery.outcome: The adopter required-checks seed is a template rather than the hub's own live instance, the adoption-time derivation fires on it, and the gate refuses an instance that describes a different repository, so an unadapted seed can neither be produced nor kept silently.
nonGoals: No rewrite of the 30 affected instances; adopting this revision repairs them through the existing derivation.
No new repair mechanism: create_adoption_lock.py already projected the declaration from the target's workflows and only needed the marker wired in.
No schema change; the marker satisfies the existing owner/name pattern.

architecture.decision: Seed from template/files like every other adopter file, and reuse the derivation that already repairs a hub-identity declaration during adoption by widening its trigger to the template marker. Keep the legacy source in both extendable allowlists so a repository pinned before this change still validates while it upgrades. The gate resolves identity from the origin remote, falling back to GITHUB_REPOSITORY, because the remote is what other participants address the repository by.
interfaceChanges: The adopter seed for .governance/required-checks.json is template/files/required-checks.template.json and carries the identity marker unresolved/adopter.
check_required_checks.py now fails closed when the instance declares a repository other than this checkout's origin or still carries the marker.
architecture.rollback: Repoint the manifest source back to governance/required-checks.json, narrow the derivation trigger and drop the identity check; the legacy source is already accepted everywhere.

validation.evidence: Measured across 88 governed checkouts: 30 declare wellmanifest/new-project while living elsewhere, 22 require the hub's job names test and windows-governance, and zero managed files drifted. The adoption fixture proves a fresh adoption now projects the declaration from the target's own workflows, so the marker never survives adoption.
